messages:
maria.g: Hey team, after upgrading our SDK we're getting 400 from /v1/embeddings. Error in response: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 768". I only changed the client, not the model. Any ideas?

sam.support: Can you paste the exact request body (raw)? Most of these are single vs batch encoding issues or double-wrapped arrays. Also which model are you hitting?

maria.g: We're calling model "text-embed-002" (internal alias). Here's the curl we send from our service (redacted keys):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "This is a test to embed", "model": "text-embed-002"}'
```

Not sure why dims differ, we were getting 1536 before.

sam.support: There it is — your payload is a single string. The embeddings endpoint expects either a single-element array or a batch array. The correct body is: {"input": ["This is a test to embed"], "model": "text-embed-002"}. Sending a raw string sometimes maps to a different legacy model path that returns 768 dims. Also double-check your client isn't wrapping again.

tomas.eng: Another common gotcha: our in-house helper did `inputs = arr.map(JSON.stringify)` then `body = JSON.stringify({input: inputs})` and someone later passed `body` through a fetch wrapper that JSON.stringified the whole thing again -> you end up with `[["text"]]`. That produces the wrong shape.

maria.g: Ah ok, we do have a wrapper. I grepped and found we were accidentally doing JSON.stringify twice when sending through our telemetry proxy. Good catch.

sam.support: If you can repro, try this minimal curl to confirm server behavior (should return 1536-dim vec):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": ["hello world"], "model": "text-embed-002"}' | jq .
```

sam.support: If that works, then instrument your client to log the outgoing request body before the proxy. Look for extra brackets or `"[\"...\"]"` (a stringified JSON array).

maria.g: Logged it — our telemetry proxy was stringifying bodies to stash them, so the network call ended up with "input": "[\"This is a test to embed\"]". Fixing that to pass a real array fixed the 400 immediately.

tomas.eng: fwiw, if you expect to send variable batches, either always send an array (even for single items) or normalize server-side. Also watch max batch size — huge arrays can cause latency spikes/429s if you hit rate limits.

maria.g: Thanks all — wrapping inputs in an array and removing the extra stringify fixed it. Leaving a note in our repo and adding a unit test to assert request body is JSON, not a string. :thumbsup:

embed-bot: Tip: use the /debug/echo endpoint in staging to validate raw requests before hitting production endpoints.
